name: Thomas Gottstein

summary.text: Thomas Gottstein was Group CEO of Credit Suisse from 2020 until he stepped down on 1 August 2022, citing personal and health-related considerations. During his tenure the bank lost more than $5 billion on the March 2021 collapse of Archegos Capital Management, and an outside review by Paul, Weiss commissioned by the bank was published in July 2021.

facts.claim: Credit Suisse's exposure to Archegos was about $20 billion; Gottstein and chief risk officer Lara Warner became aware of the exposure in the days before the forced liquidation of March 2021.
facts.quote: Gottstein and Lara Warner, the bank's recently departed chief risk officer, became aware of the Archegos exposure in the days leading up to the forced liquidation

sources.title: Credit Suisse report on Archegos loss points to a massive culture problem

facts.claim: In April 2021 Gottstein called the Archegos loss 'unacceptable' and said the bank had to take actions in terms of management changes.

The 172-page Paul, Weiss review of Credit Suisse's Archegos business, released in late July 2021, found it likely that Archegos deceived the bank and obscured the extent of its positions, placed much of the blame on junior staff and found no evidence of fraud or malicious intent inside the bank.
